sentences.zh: 25%◎蘇尹畢李鄭王許潘倪席齊=蘇向=蘇向，雍州藍田人。

translations.literal: Volume 128 Biographies 53: Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, Qi — Su Xiang. Su Xiang was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 128, Biographies 53: Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, and Qi — Su Xiang. Su Xiang came from Lantian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中明經第，調鄠尉。

translations.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination and was appointed aide at Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as aide at Hu County.

sentences.zh: 時李義琰為雍州長史，鄠多訟，日至長史府，恦裁決明辦，自是無訴者。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yiyan was chief secretary of Yong Prefecture; Hu had many lawsuits, and people came daily to the chief secretary's office — Xiang's judgments were clear and decisive, and from then on there were no litigants.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyan was then chief secretary of Yong Prefecture. Hu County was rife with lawsuits, and people came every day to the chief secretary's office. Xiang's rulings were lucid and decisive, and after that there were no more complainants.

sentences.zh: 義琰異之，顧聽事曰：「此公坐也，恨吾齒晚，不及見。」

translations.literal: Yiyan marveled at him, glanced toward the hall and said, "This is the gentleman's seat; I regret my years came late and I could not meet him sooner."
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan was struck by his ability. Glancing toward the reception hall, he said, "That is this gentleman's seat — I only wish I had not grown old so soon and could have known him earlier."

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era, he became investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chuigong period he was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 武後殺韓、魯諸王，付向密牒按訊，向推之無狀。

translations.literal: Empress Wu killed the princes of Han and Lu and handed Xiang a secret dossier to investigate; Xiang pursued it and found no evidence.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu executed the Han and Lu princes, she gave Xiang a secret dossier to investigate them. He pursued the case and found nothing to support the charges.

sentences.zh: 或言向助韓、魯者，後詰之，挺議無所撓，後不悅曰：「卿，大雅士，此獄不足諉卿。」

translations.literal: Some said Xiang had aided the Han and Lu; the Empress questioned him; he stood firm in argument without yielding; she said displeasedly, "You are a man of great refinement; this case is not enough to implicate you."
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed Xiang had helped the Han and Lu princes. The Empress questioned him, but he argued his case without bending. Displeased, she said, "You are a man of the highest refinement — this case is not enough to blame you."

sentences.zh: 即詔監軍河西。

translations.literal: She immediately ordered him to supervise the army in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: She at once ordered him to supervise troops in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 五遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became right section director.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he rose to director of the right section.

sentences.zh: 御史王弘義附來俊臣為酷，世畏疾，莫敢觸其鋒。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Hongyi attached himself to Lai Junchen in cruelty; the age feared and detested him, and none dared touch his edge.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Wang Hongyi joined Lai Junchen in his reign of terror. The world feared and loathed him, and no one dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 會督伐材於虢，笞督過程，人多死，向按奏，弘義坐免。

translations.literal: When supervising timber-cutting in Guo, he flogged the supervisors beyond measure and many died; Xiang memorialized against him and Hongyi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while supervising timber-cutting in Guo, Hongyi beat the overseers so severely during the work that many died. Xiang investigated and memorialized against him, and Hongyi was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，進左肅政臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant within the palace gates and advanced to censor-in-chief of the Left Office for Scrutinizing Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and then to censor-in-chief of the Left Office for Scrutinizing Governance.

sentences.zh: 後營大像白司馬阪，糜用億計，向上疏切諫，見納。

translations.literal: The Empress built a great image at White Horse Slope; expenditures ran to hundreds of millions; Xiang submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance and it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress undertook the great Buddha image at White Horse Slope, costs mounted into the hundreds of millions. Xiang submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, and it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 中宗將斬韋月將，向執據時令不可以大戮，忤三思意，改右臺，俄出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was about to execute Wei Yuejiang, Xiang held to the seasonal statutes that capital punishment was not permitted and offended Wu Sansi's wishes; he was moved to the right censorate and soon sent out as prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was about to execute Wei Yuejiang, Xiang insisted that the seasonal statutes forbade capital punishment at that time, offending Wu Sansi. He was shifted to the right censorate and soon sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復為右臺大夫。

translations.literal: He again became censor-in-chief of the right censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made censor-in-chief of the right censorate.

sentences.zh: 會節湣太子敗，詔株索支黨。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jiemin was overthrown, an edict ordered the rooting out of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin fell, an edict went out to hunt down his associates.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗居藩，為獄辭牽逮，向密啟保辯，亦會宰相開陳，帝感悟，多所含貸。

translations.literal: At that time Ruizong was in his princely residence and was implicated by trial records; Xiang secretly memorialized to protect and defend him; the chief ministers also spoke plainly; the Emperor was moved and showed much forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong was then in his princely residence and was dragged in by the indictments. Xiang secretly memorialized in his defense, and the chief ministers also spoke plainly. The Emperor took the point and showed much forbearance.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部尚書，封河內郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of revenue and enfeoffed as Duke of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of revenue and enfeoffed as Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 以檢校太子詹事致仕。

translations.literal: He retired with the acting title of steward of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the acting title of steward of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一，贈兗州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-one; posthumously made area commander of Yanzhou; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one. He was posthumously made area commander of Yan Prefecture, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子晉，數歲知為文，作《八卦論》，吏部侍郎房潁叔、秘書少監王紹宗嘆曰：「後來之王粲也。

translations.literal: His son Jin, while still a few years old, knew how to write; he composed "Discourse on the Eight Trigrams"; Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Yingshu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Shaozong exclaimed, "A Wang Can for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin could write while still a child. He composed the "Discourse on the Eight Trigrams." Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Yingshu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Shaozong exclaimed, "Here is a Wang Can for our own day.

sentences.zh: 舉進士及大禮科，皆上第。

translations.literal: He took the jinshi and the great ritual examinations and placed at the top in both.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both the jinshi examination and the great ritual examination at the top of each.

sentences.zh: 先天中，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era he became drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian period he served as drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄宗監國，所下制命，多晉及賈曾稿。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong supervised the state, most of the edicts and orders issued were drafted by Jin and Jia Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was regent, most of the edicts and orders issued were drafted by Jin and Jia Zeng.

sentences.zh: 屢獻讜言，天子嘉允。

translations.literal: He repeatedly offered forthright counsel; the Son of Heaven commended and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly offered forthright counsel, and the emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 出為泗州刺史，以向老，請解職奉養。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Si; because Xiang was old, he requested to leave office to support and care for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Si. When his father Xiang grew old, he asked to resign and return home to support him.

sentences.zh: 向卒，歷戶部侍郎，襲爵，遷吏部。

translations.literal: After Xiang died, he served as vice minister of revenue, inherited the title, and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang died, he served as vice minister of revenue, inherited his father's title, and was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時宋璟兼尚書事，晉與齊浣更典二都選，既糊名校判，而晉獨事賞拔，當時譽之。

translations.literal: At that time Song Jing also held charge of the ministries; Jin and Qi Huan alternated in managing selection for the two capitals; after names were pasted over for blind review, Jin alone handled rewards and promotions, and the age praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing was then also in charge of the ministries. Jin and Qi Huan took turns managing recruitment for the two capitals. After the names were sealed for blind review, Jin alone handled commendation and promotion, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及裴光庭知尚書，有過官被卻者，就籍以朱點頭而已。

translations.literal: When Pei Guangting took charge of the ministries, candidates who had faults were simply marked with a red dot on the register.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Guangting took charge of the ministries, candidates who had been rejected were simply marked with a red dot on the register.

sentences.zh: 晉因榜選院曰「門下點頭者更擬」，光庭以為侮己，出晉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Jin therefore posted at the selection office, "Those marked with a nod by the gate may be reconsidered"; Guangting took this as an insult to himself and sent Jin out as prefect of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Jin posted a notice at the selection office: "Those the gate has nodded at may be reconsidered." Guangting took this as a personal insult and sent Jin out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷魏州，終太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wei Prefecture and ended as left aide to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wei Prefecture and ended his career as left aide to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始，晉與洛人張循之、仲之兄弟善，而二人以學顯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin had been on good terms with the Luoyang men Zhang Xunzhi and the brothers Zhongzhi, and the two had become famous through learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had long been close to the Luoyang scholars Zhang Xunzhi and the brothers Zhongzhi, both of whom had won renown through learning.

sentences.zh: 循之上書忤武後，見殺。

translations.literal: Xunzhi submitted a memorial that offended Empress Wu and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi submitted a memorial that offended Empress Wu and was executed.

sentences.zh: 仲之神龍中謀去武三思，為宋之愻等所發，死，晉厚撫其子漸，為營婚宦。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era Zhongzhi plotted to remove Wu Sansi; he was exposed by Song Zhisun and others and died; Jin treated his son Jian generously and arranged marriage and office for him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong period Zhongzhi plotted to remove Wu Sansi, was exposed by Song Zhisun and others, and was put to death. Jin treated his son Jian generously and arranged marriage and an official career for him.

sentences.zh: 晉卒，漸喪之若諸父雲。

translations.literal: When Jin died, Jian mourned him as if for an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin died, Jian mourned him as he would an uncle.

sentences.zh: =尹思貞=尹思貞，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yin Sizhen. Yin Sizhen was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Sizhen. Yin Sizhen came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 弱冠以明經第，調隆州參軍事。

translations.literal: In his youth he placed in the Mingjing examination and was appointed military adjutant in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as military adjutant in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬邑豪蒲氏驁肆不法，州檄思貞按之，擿其奸贓萬計，卒論死，部人稱慶，刻石嘆頌。

translations.literal: A local magnate of the Pu clan in his district was arrogant and lawless; the prefecture ordered Sizhen to investigate; he exposed tens of thousands in illicit gains; Pu was finally sentenced to death; the people rejoiced and carved stone in praise.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate of the Pu clan in his district was arrogant and lawless. The prefecture ordered Sizhen to investigate. He exposed tens of thousands in illicit gains, and Pu was finally sentenced to death. The people rejoiced and carved a stone inscription in praise.

sentences.zh: 遷明堂令，以善政聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Bright Hall district and became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Bright Hall district and became known for good governance.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中少監，檢校洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the palace workshops and acting prefect of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the palace workshops and made acting prefect of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會契丹孫萬榮亂，朔方震驚，思貞循撫境內，獨無擾。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Sun Wanrong rebelled and the north was shaken, Sizhen soothed and comforted his territory alone without disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Sun Wanrong rebelled and the north was thrown into alarm, Sizhen alone kept his jurisdiction calm through patient governance.

sentences.zh: 武後璽書褒慰。

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent an imperial letter of commendation and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent an imperial letter praising and comforting him.

sentences.zh: 長安中，遷秋官侍郎，忤張昌宗意，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was transferred to vice minister of justice; he offended Zhang Changzong's wishes and was sent out as prefect of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period he was made vice minister of justice. He offended Zhang Changzong and was sent out as prefect of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召授司府少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed vice minister of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 時卿侯知一亦厲威嚴，吏為語曰：「不畏侯卿杖，祗畏尹卿筆。」

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Hou Zhiyi was also severe in authority; the clerks had a saying: "We do not fear Vice Minister Hou's staff — we only fear Vice Minister Yin's brush."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Hou Zhiyi was also severe in his authority. The clerks had a saying: "We do not fear Vice Minister Hou's staff — we only fear Vice Minister Yin's brush."

sentences.zh: 加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 其家坎地，獲古戟十二，俄而門樹戟，時人異焉。

translations.literal: At his home they dug the ground and found twelve ancient halberds; soon halberds grew on the gate tree, and people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When his household dug the ground, they found twelve ancient halberds. Soon halberds appeared on the tree at his gate, and contemporaries took it as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，擢大理卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted to chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong period he was promoted to chief of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 雍人韋月將告武三思大逆，中宗命斬之，思貞以方發生月，固奏不可，乃決杖，流嶺南。

translations.literal: The Yong man Wei Yuejiang reported Wu Sansi's great treason; Zhongzong ordered his execution; Sizhen held that the season when the moon was just waxing forbade it and firmly memorialized that it could not be done; he was therefore beaten with the rod and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang of Yong reported Wu Sansi's great treason. Emperor Zhongzong ordered his execution. Sizhen held that capital punishment was forbidden while the moon was just waxing and firmly memorialized against it. Wei was beaten with the rod instead and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 三思諷所司加法殺之，復固爭，禦中大夫李承嘉助三思，而以他事劾思貞，不得謁。

translations.literal: Sansi prompted the authorities to add to the penalty and execute him; Sizhen again argued firmly; Palace Attendant Li Chengjia aided Sansi and impeached Sizhen on another matter, and he was denied audience.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi prompted the authorities to increase the penalty and execute Wei. Sizhen argued again. Palace Attendant Li Chengjia sided with Sansi and impeached Sizhen on another charge, and he was denied audience at court.

sentences.zh: 思貞謂承嘉曰「公為天子執法，乃擅威福，慢憲度，諛附奸臣圖不軌，今將除忠良以自恣邪？」

translations.literal: Sizhen said to Chengjia, "You enforce the law for the Son of Heaven, yet you usurp authority and favor, slight the statutes, and fawn on traitors plotting sedition — will you now remove the loyal and good to indulge yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen said to Chengjia, "You enforce the law for the Son of Heaven, yet you usurp authority, slight the statutes, and fawn on traitors plotting sedition. Will you now remove the loyal and good to indulge yourself?"

sentences.zh: 承嘉慚怒，劾思貞，為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Chengjia, ashamed and angry, impeached Sizhen and made him prefect of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia, ashamed and furious, impeached Sizhen and had him sent out as prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「公敏行，何與承嘉辯？」

translations.literal: Someone asked, "You are a man of quick action — why debate with Chengjia?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "You are a man of quick action — why debate with Chengjia?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「石非能言者，而或有言。

translations.literal: He answered, "Stone is not something that can speak, yet sometimes it speaks.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Stone cannot speak, yet sometimes it does.

sentences.zh: 承嘉恃權而侮吾，義不辱，亦不知言何從而至。」

translations.literal: Chengjia relied on power to insult me; by principle I could not endure disgrace, and I do not know whence the words came."
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia relied on power to insult me. By principle I could not endure disgrace, and I do not know where the words came from."

sentences.zh: 治州有績，蠶至歲四熟，黜陟使路敬潛至部，嘆曰：「是非善政致祥乎！」

translations.literal: In governing the prefecture he had achievement; silkworms matured four times in a year; the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Lu Jingqian came to the circuit and exclaimed, "Is this not good government bringing auspicious signs!"
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture with distinction. Silkworms matured four times in one year. The promotion-and-demotion commissioner Lu Jingqian came to the circuit and exclaimed, "Is this not good government bringing auspicious signs!"

sentences.zh: 表言之。

translations.literal: He memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized about it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，召授將作大匠，封天水郡公。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed director of palace construction and enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Sizhen was summoned and appointed director of palace construction and enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 僕射竇懷貞護作金仙、玉真觀，廣調夫匠，思貞數有損節。

translations.literal: Pushe Dou Huai'zhen supervised construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfection abbeys and broadly conscripted laborers; Sizhen repeatedly made reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Dou Huai'zhen supervised construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfection abbeys and broadly conscripted laborers. Sizhen repeatedly cut the quotas.

sentences.zh: 懷貞讓之，答曰：「公，輔臣也，不能宣贊王化，而土木是興，以媚上害下，又聽小人譖以廷辱士，今不可事公矣。」

translations.literal: Huai'zhen reproached him; he answered, "You are a chief minister, yet you cannot proclaim and assist royal transformation, while you raise earth and timber to flatter those above and harm those below, and you heed petty men's slanders to humiliate gentlemen in court — I can no longer serve you."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'zhen reproached him. He answered, "You are a chief minister, yet you cannot proclaim and assist royal transformation while you raise earth and timber to flatter those above and harm those below, and you heed petty men's slanders to humiliate gentlemen at court. I can no longer serve you."

sentences.zh: 乃拂衣去，闔門待罪。

translations.literal: He then shook out his robes and left, shutting his gate to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He shook out his robes and left, shutting his gate to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，特詔令視事。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of it and specially ordered him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and specially ordered him to resume office.

sentences.zh: 懷貞誅，拜御史大夫，累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Huai'zhen was executed, he was appointed censor-in-chief and after repeated promotions became minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'zhen was executed, he was appointed censor-in-chief and eventually rose to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: He requested retirement and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 開元四年卒，年七十七，贈黃門監，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Kaiyuan at age seventy-seven; posthumously made overseer of the Yellow Gate; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaiyuan at seventy-seven. He was posthumously made overseer of the Yellow Gate, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 思貞前後為刺史十三郡，其政皆以清最聞。

translations.literal: Sizhen served as prefect in thirteen commanderies in all; his governance in each was known for purity at the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen served as prefect in thirteen commanderies altogether, and in each his governance was known for exceptional purity.

sentences.zh: =畢構=畢構，字隆擇，河南偃師人。

translations.literal: Bi Gou. Bi Gou, courtesy name Longze, was a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gou. Bi Gou, courtesy name Longze, came from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 六歲能為文。

translations.literal: At six he could write.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could already write.

sentences.zh: 及冠，擢進士第，補金水尉，遷九隴主簿。

translations.literal: Upon reaching adulthood he placed in the jinshi examination, was appointed aide at Jinshui, and was transferred to chief clerk of Jiulong.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed aide at Jinshui, and was transferred to chief clerk of Jiulong.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，毀棘甚，已除，猶屏處丘園。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his parents his grief was extreme; even after the mourning period ended he still secluded himself in garden and field.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his parents his grief was extreme. Even after the mourning period ended he still secluded himself in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 武後召為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned him as left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned him as left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was transferred to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong period he was made drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等表諸武不宜為王，構當讀表，抗聲析句，左右皆曉知。

translations.literal: Jing Hui and others submitted a memorial that the Wu clan should not be made princes; Gou was to read the memorial and parsed the sentences in a ringing voice so that all present understood.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui and others submitted a memorial arguing that the Wu clan should not be made princes. Gou was assigned to read it aloud, parsing each sentence in a ringing voice until everyone present understood.

sentences.zh: 三思疾之，出為潤州刺史，政有惠愛。

translations.literal: Sansi resented him and sent him out as prefect of Run; his governance showed kindness and care.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi resented him and sent him out as prefect of Run, where his governance showed kindness and care.

sentences.zh: 徙衛、同、陜三州，遷益州府長史。

translations.literal: He was moved through the three prefectures of Wei, Tong, and Shan, and was transferred to chief administrator of Yizhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession at Wei, Tong, and Shan prefectures, then was made chief administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，召為左御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong he was summoned as left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinglong period he was summoned as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 會平諸韋，治其黨，衣冠多坐，構詳比重輕，皆得其情。

translations.literal: When the various Wei were suppressed, he tried their faction; many officials and gentry were implicated; Gou weighed severity and leniency in detail and in each case grasped the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction was suppressed, he tried their associates. Many officials and gentry were implicated. Gou weighed severity and leniency in detail and in each case grasped the facts.

sentences.zh: 時李傑為河南尹，與構皆一時選，世謂「畢李」。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jie was intendant of Henan; he and Gou were both men of the finest selection of the age, and the world called them "Bi and Li."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie was then intendant of Henan. He and Gou were both regarded as the finest men of their day, and people called them "Bi and Li."

sentences.zh: 封魏縣男。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wei county.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 復為益州長史，按察劍南，振弊柅私，號為清嚴。

translations.literal: He again became chief administrator of Yizhou and inspected Jiannan; he shook off abuses and checked private interests and was styled pure and severe.
translations.idiomatic: He again became chief administrator of Yizhou and inspected Jiannan. He shook off abuses, checked private interests, and was known for purity and severity.

sentences.zh: 睿宗嘉構脩罝獨行，有古人風，其治術又為諸使最，乃賜璽書、袍帶。

translations.literal: Ruizong commended Gou's cultivated conduct and independent integrity, which had the air of antiquity; his methods of governance were also foremost among all commissioners; he was therefore granted an imperial letter and robe and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong praised Gou's cultivated conduct and independent integrity, which had the air of antiquity, and his methods of governance were also foremost among all commissioners. He was therefore granted an imperial letter, robe, and belt.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部尚書，並遙領益州長史，徙廣州都督。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to minister of personnel and also held Yizhou chief administrator in absentia, then was moved to area commander of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made minister of personnel while also holding Yizhou chief administrator in absentia, then was moved to area commander of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄宗立，授河南尹，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he was appointed intendant of Henan and advanced to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, Gou was appointed intendant of Henan and promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 久之，移疾，帝手疏醫方賜之。

translations.literal: After a long time he reported illness; the Emperor personally wrote out a medical prescription and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he reported illness, and the emperor personally wrote out a medical prescription and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 當時以戶部為兇官，遽改太子詹事，冀其愈。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of Revenue was considered an ill-omened office; he was quickly changed to steward of the crown prince's household in hope that he would recover.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was then considered an ill-omened office, so he was quickly made steward of the crown prince's household in hope that he would recover.

sentences.zh: 會卒，贈黃門監，謚曰景。

translations.literal: He soon died; posthumously made overseer of the Yellow Gate; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died. He was posthumously made overseer of the Yellow Gate, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 始，構喪繼母，而二妹繈褓，身鞠養至成人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gou lost his stepmother, his two younger sisters were still in swaddling clothes; he personally reared and nurtured them until they reached adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou lost his stepmother, his two younger sisters were still infants. He personally reared them until they reached adulthood.

sentences.zh: 妹為構服三年。

translations.literal: The sisters wore mourning for Gou for three years.
translations.idiomatic: His sisters wore mourning for him for three years.

sentences.zh: 弟栩，以太府主簿留司東都，聞疾馳歸，哀毀如大喪，雖變服未嘗笑，天下稱其友悌。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu, as chief clerk of the palace treasury remaining on duty in the eastern capital, heard of the illness and raced home; his grief was as for a parent's death; though he had changed out of mourning garb he never smiled; the world praised his friendship and fraternal duty.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was chief clerk of the palace treasury on duty in the eastern capital. When he heard Gou was ill, he raced home. His grief was as for a parent's death, and though he had changed out of mourning garb he never smiled. The world praised his friendship and fraternal duty.

sentences.zh: 終荊州司馬。

translations.literal: He ended as military aide of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as military aide of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 構子炕，天寶末為廣平太守，拒安祿山，城陷，覆其家。

translations.literal: Gou's son Kang, at the end of Tianbao was prefect of Guangping; he resisted An Lushan; the city fell and his whole household was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's son Kang was prefect of Guangping at the end of the Tianbao era. He resisted An Lushan, but the city fell and his whole household was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously made minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 炕生，始四歲，與弟增以細弱得不殺，為賞口。

translations.literal: Kang's son Sheng, only four years old, and his younger brother Zeng, because they were small and weak were not killed and were taken as reward captives.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Sheng was only four years old. He and his younger brother Zeng were spared because they were small and weak, and were taken as reward captives.

sentences.zh: 河北平，宗人宏以財贖出之。

translations.literal: When Hebei was pacified, his clansman Hong redeemed them with wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was pacified, their clansman Hong redeemed them with money.

sentences.zh: 後舉明經，為臨渙尉。

translations.literal: Later he took the Mingjing examination and became aide at Linhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed aide at Linhuan.

sentences.zh: 徐州節度使張建封高炕節，聞篤行，表署幕府，攝符離令。

translations.literal: Xuzhou military governor Zhang Jianfeng admired Kang's integrity; hearing of Sheng's earnest conduct, he memorialized to appoint him to the staff and had him act as magistrate of Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou military governor Zhang Jianfeng admired Kang's integrity. Hearing of Sheng's earnest conduct, he memorialized to appoint him to his staff and had him act as magistrate of Fuli.

sentences.zh: 後調王屋尉，以謹廉聞。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to aide at Wangwu and became known for prudence and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to aide at Wangwu and became known for prudence and integrity.

sentences.zh: 喜賓客，家未嘗以有無計。

translations.literal: He delighted in guests; his household never reckoned by having or not having.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in entertaining guests, and his household never counted its wealth.

sentences.zh: 及歿，無貲以治喪雲。

translations.literal: When he died there were no funds to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died there was not enough money even to conduct his funeral.

sentences.zh: =李傑=李傑，本名務光，相州釜陽人。

translations.literal: Li Jie. Li Jie, original name Wuguang, was a native of Fuyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie. Li Jie, whose original name was Wuguang, came from Fuyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後魏并州刺史寶之裔孫。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Bao, area commander of Bingzhou in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Bao, the area commander of Bing Prefecture under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 少以孝友著。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，解褐齊州參軍事，遷累天官員外郎。

translations.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination, left the commoner's garb as military adjutant in Qi Prefecture, and after repeated promotions became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination, entered service as military adjutant in Qi Prefecture, and after repeated promotions became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 為吏詳敏，有治譽。

translations.literal: As an official he was thorough and quick, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: As an official he was thorough and quick, and won a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 以采訪使行山南，時戶口逋蕩，細弱下戶為豪力所兼，傑為設科條區處，檢防亡匿，復業者十七八。

translations.literal: As investigating commissioner he toured Shannan; at the time household registers were scattered and the weak and low-status households were absorbed by powerful men; Jie set up regulations to sort them out, inspected against flight and concealment, and seven or eight tenths returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: As investigating commissioner he toured Shannan. Household registers were then in disarray, and weak, low-status households were being absorbed by powerful men. Jie set up regulations to sort them out, inspected against flight and concealment, and seven or eight tenths of those displaced returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，為河東巡察黜陟使，課最諸道。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was promotion-and-demotion commissioner inspecting Hedong; his assessment ranked highest among all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong period he was promotion-and-demotion commissioner inspecting Hedong, and his assessment ranked highest among all circuits.

sentences.zh: 先天中，進陜州刺史、水陸發運使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era he was advanced to prefect of Shan and commissioner for water and land transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian period he was promoted to prefect of Shan and commissioner for water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 置使自傑始。

translations.literal: The establishment of this commissioner began with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The office of transport commissioner was first established with Jie.

sentences.zh: 改河南尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 傑既精聽斷，雖行坐食飲，省治不少廢，繇是府無淹事，人吏愛之。

translations.literal: Jie was skilled in hearing cases and judging; even while walking, sitting, eating, or drinking he did not slacken in his office work; therefore the prefecture had no backlog, and officials and clerks loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was skilled at hearing cases and rendering judgment. Even while walking, sitting, eating, or drinking he never slackened in his office work. The prefecture therefore had no backlog, and officials and clerks loved him.

sentences.zh: 寡婦有告其子不孝者，傑物色非是，謂婦曰：「子法當死，無悔乎？」

translations.literal: A widow reported that her son was unfilial; Jie observed that this was not so and said to the woman, "By law your son should die — do you not regret it?"
translations.idiomatic: A widow reported that her son was unfilial. Jie observed that this was not so and said to the woman, "By law your son should die. Will you not regret it?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「子無狀，寧其悔！」

translations.literal: She answered, "The son is worthless — how could I regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "The boy is worthless — why would I regret it!"

sentences.zh: 乃命市棺還斂之，使人跡婦出，與一道士語，頃持棺至，傑令捕道士按問，乃與婦私不得逞。

translations.literal: He then ordered a coffin bought and had the son reinterred; he had someone follow the woman when she went out and found her speaking with a Daoist priest; soon the priest arrived with the coffin; Jie ordered the priest seized and interrogated — he and the woman had been lovers and could not have their way.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a coffin bought and had the son reinterred. He had someone follow the woman when she went out and found her speaking with a Daoist priest. Soon the priest arrived with the coffin. Jie ordered the priest seized and interrogated — he and the woman had been lovers and could not have their way.

sentences.zh: 傑殺道士，內於棺。

translations.literal: Jie killed the priest and placed him inside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Jie killed the priest and placed him inside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 河、汴之交舊有梁公埭，廢不治，南方漕弗通，傑調汴、鄭丁男復作之，不費而利。

translations.literal: At the junction of the Yellow and Bian rivers there had been the Liang Duke's embankment, abandoned and unrepaired so that southern grain transport could not pass; Jie conscripted adult males from Bian and Zheng to rebuild it, with benefit and no waste.
translations.idiomatic: At the junction of the Yellow and Bian rivers there had been the Liang Duke's embankment, abandoned and unrepaired so that southern grain transport could not pass. Jie conscripted adult males from Bian and Zheng to rebuild it, to great benefit and at little cost.

sentences.zh: 入代宋璟為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He entered office to replace Song Jing as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Song Jing as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尚衣奉禦長孫昕素惡傑，遇於道，內恃玄宗婭婿，與所親楊仙玉共毆辱之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant of Imperial Wardrobe Changsun Xin had long hated Jie; they met on the road; relying inwardly on being Xuanzong's son-in-law, he and his intimate Yang Xianyu together beat and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant of Imperial Wardrobe Changsun Xin had long hated Jie. They met on the road, and Changsun, relying on being Emperor Xuanzong's son-in-law, together with his intimate Yang Xianyu beat and humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 傑訴曰：「敗髮膚，痛在身；

translations.literal: Jie appealed, saying, "To injure hair and skin causes pain in the body;
translations.idiomatic: Jie appealed, saying, "To injure hair and skin causes pain in the body;

sentences.zh: 辱衣冠，恥在國。」

translations.literal: to insult official robes and caps brings shame to the state."
translations.idiomatic: to insult official robes and caps brings shame to the state."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔斬昕等朝堂。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered Xin and the others beheaded in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered Xin and the others beheaded in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍馬懷素建言：「陽和月，不可以殊死。」

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant Ma Huaisu offered counsel: "In the month of yang harmony, extraordinary death penalties may not be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Left Regular Attendant Ma Huaisu offered counsel: "In the month of yang harmony, extraordinary death penalties may not be carried out."

sentences.zh: 乃敕杖殺之，謝百官，降書慰傑。

translations.literal: He then ordered them beaten to death with the rod, apologized to the hundred officials, and sent down a letter to comfort Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered them beaten to death with the rod, apologized to the hundred officials, and sent down a letter to comfort Jie.

sentences.zh: 以護作橋陵，封武威縣子。

translations.literal: For supervising construction of Qiaoling he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuwei county.
translations.idiomatic: For supervising construction of Qiaoling he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuwei County.

sentences.zh: 初，傑引侍御史王旭為護陵判官，旭貪贓，傑將繩之，未及發，反為所構，出衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier Jie had brought in Attending Censor Wang Xu as judge for protecting the tomb; Xu was corrupt; Jie was about to punish him but before he could act was instead framed by him and sent out as prefect of Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jie had brought in Attending Censor Wang Xu as judge for protecting the tomb. Xu was corrupt, and Jie was about to punish him, but before he could act was instead framed by Xu and sent out as prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷揚州大都督府長史，復為御史劾免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and again was impeached by censors and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and was again impeached by censors and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 開元六年卒，帝悼之，特贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Kaiyuan; the Emperor mourned him and specially posthumously made him minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Kaiyuan. The emperor mourned him and specially posthumously made him minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: =鄭惟忠=鄭惟忠，宋州宋城人。

translations.literal: Zheng Weizhong. Zheng Weizhong was a native of Songcheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weizhong. Zheng Weizhong came from Songcheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補井陘尉。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was appointed aide at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed aide at Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 天授中，以制舉召見廷中，武後問舉者，何所事為忠，對皆不合旨。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era he was summoned by decree examination and received in the hall; Empress Wu asked the examinees what acts constituted loyalty; their answers all failed to match her intent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou period he was summoned by decree examination and received in the hall. Empress Wu asked the examinees what acts constituted loyalty, and their answers all failed to match her intent.

sentences.zh: 惟忠曰：「外揚君之美，內正君之惡。」

translations.literal: Weizhong said, "Outwardly to proclaim the ruler's excellence, inwardly to correct the ruler's faults."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong said, "Outwardly to proclaim the ruler's excellence, inwardly to correct the ruler's faults."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 擢左司禦胄曹參軍事，遷水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military adjutant in the Left Office for Imperial Guard Equipment and transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military adjutant in the Left Office for Imperial Guard Equipment and transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 後還長安，復以待制召。

translations.literal: When the Empress returned to Chang'an he was again summoned as awaiting imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress returned to Chang'an he was again summoned as awaiting imperial command.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「非嘗於東都對忠臣者乎？

translations.literal: The Empress said, "Are you not the one who answered about the loyal minister at the eastern capital?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Are you not the one who answered about the loyal minister at the eastern capital?

sentences.zh: 朕今不忘。」

translations.literal: I have not forgotten you now."
translations.idiomatic: I have not forgotten you."

sentences.zh: 遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to drafting secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to drafting secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，擢黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne he was promoted to vice minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne he was promoted to vice minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時議禁嶺南酋戶不得畜兵，惟忠曰：「善為政者因其俗。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of forbidding tribal households in Lingnan to keep weapons; Weizhong said, "One who governs well follows local custom.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was discussion of forbidding tribal households in Lingnan to keep weapons. Weizhong said, "One who governs well follows local custom.

sentences.zh: 且吳人所謂家鶴膝、戶犀渠，此民風也，禁之得無擾乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover what the people of Wu call 'crane-knee in every home' and 'rhinoceros-horn channel in every household' — this is local custom; would forbidding it not cause disturbance?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover what the people of Wu call 'crane-knee in every home' and 'rhinoceros-horn channel in every household' is local custom. Would forbidding it not cause disturbance?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The proposal was therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was therefore dropped.

sentences.zh: 進大理卿。

translations.literal: He was advanced to chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子敗，守衛詿誤皆流，已決，諸韋黨請悉誅之，帝欲改推。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jiemin was overthrown, the guards who had been implicated by error were all exiled; the sentence had already been decided; the Wei faction asked that all be executed; the Emperor wished to reopen the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin fell, the guards who had been implicated by error were all exiled and the sentence had already been decided. The Wei faction asked that all be executed, and the emperor wished to reopen the case.

sentences.zh: 惟忠奏：「大獄始判，復改訊，恐反側者不自安，且失信天下。」

translations.literal: Weizhong memorialized: "A great case has just been decided; to reopen interrogation will make those who have wavered feel unsafe and moreover lose the trust of the empire."
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong memorialized: "A great case has just been decided. To reopen interrogation will make those who have wavered feel unsafe and will lose the trust of the empire."

sentences.zh: 有詔百司參議，卒論如前，所全貸為多。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred offices to confer; the final judgment remained as before, and many were spared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the hundred offices to confer. The final judgment remained as before, and many were spared.

sentences.zh: 俄授御史大夫，持節賑給河北道，且許黜陟守宰。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed censor-in-chief, bearing credentials to provide relief on the Hebei circuit and also permitted to promote or demote prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed censor-in-chief, bearing credentials to provide relief on the Hebei circuit and also permitted to promote or demote prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 還奏稱旨，封滎陽縣男，遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: On his return his memorial matched the Emperor's intent; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xingyang county and transferred to companion of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On his return his memorial matched the emperor's intent. He was enfeoffed as Baron of Xingyang County and transferred to companion of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made junior guardian of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior guardian of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: =王誌愔=王誌愔，博州聊城人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiyin. Wang Zhiyin was a native of Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyin. Wang Zhiyin came from Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍中，為左臺侍御史，以剛鷙為治，所居人吏畏詟，呼為「皂雕」。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era under Zhongzong he was attending censor of the left censorate; he governed with stern severity; officials and clerks where he served feared and trembled and called him "Black Eagle."
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong period under Emperor Zhongzong he was attending censor of the left censorate. He governed with stern severity, and officials and clerks where he served feared and trembled, calling him "Black Eagle."

sentences.zh: 遷大理正，嘗奏言：「法令者，人之堤防，不立則無所制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to senior judge of the Court of Judicial Review and once memorialized: "Laws and ordinances are the dikes and barriers of men; if they are not established there is nothing to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to senior judge of the Court of Judicial Review and once memorialized: "Laws and ordinances are the dikes and barriers of men. If they are not established there is nothing to restrain.

sentences.zh: 今大理多不奉法，以縱罪為仁，持文為苛，臣執刑典，恐且得謗。」

translations.literal: Today the Court of Judicial Review often does not follow the law, treating leniency in crime as benevolence and holding to the letter as harshness; if I enforce the penal code I fear I will be slandered."
translations.idiomatic: Today the Court of Judicial Review often does not follow the law, treating leniency in crime as benevolence and holding to the letter as harshness. If I enforce the penal code I fear I will be slandered."

sentences.zh: 遂上所著《應正論》以見誌，因規帝失。

translations.literal: He then submitted his work "Discourse on Responding to Rectitude" to show his intent and thereby admonish the Emperor's faults.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted his work "Discourse on Responding to Rectitude" to show his intent and thereby admonish the emperor's faults.

sentences.zh: 大抵以《易萃》之六二曰「引吉無咎」，謂處萃之時，己獨居正，異操而聚，獨正者危，未能以遠害。

translations.literal: Broadly he took the second line of Gathering in the Book of Changes, which says "Drawing in good fortune, no blame," to mean that in a time of gathering, when one alone holds to rectitude while others of different conduct assemble, the one who alone is upright is in peril and cannot yet keep harm at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly he took the second line of Gathering in the Book of Changes, which says "Drawing in good fortune, no blame," to mean that in a time of gathering, when one alone holds to rectitude while others of different conduct assemble, the one who alone is upright is in peril and cannot yet keep harm at a distance.

sentences.zh: 惟九五應之，乃履正迎吉，由己居下位而中正是托，期於上應之，不括囊以守祿也。

translations.literal: Only when the fifth line responds to it does one tread the path of rectitude and welcome good fortune — because one occupies the lower position and entrusts rectitude to the center, expecting response from above, and does not tie the sack closed to hold one's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the fifth line responds to it does one tread the path of rectitude and welcome good fortune — because one occupies the lower position and entrusts rectitude to the center, expecting response from above, and does not tie the sack closed merely to hold one's salary.

sentences.zh: 又言：「刑賞二柄，惟人主操之。

translations.literal: He also said: "The two handles of punishment and reward are wielded only by the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The two handles of punishment and reward are wielded only by the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『以力役法者，百姓也；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'Those who serve the law by force are the common people;'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: 'Those who serve the law by force are the common people;'

sentences.zh: 以死守法者，有司也；

translations.literal: those who uphold the law even unto death are the officials;
translations.idiomatic: those who uphold the law even unto death are the officials;

sentences.zh: 以道變法者，君上也。』

translations.literal: those who change the law by the Way are the ruler above.
translations.idiomatic: those who change the law by the Way are the ruler above.

sentences.zh: 魏遊肇為廷尉，帝私敕肇有所降恕，肇執不從，曰：『陛下自能恕之，豈可令臣曲筆也。』

translations.literal: Wei Youzhao was chief of the Court of Judicial Review; the Emperor privately ordered Youzhao to reduce or pardon someone; Youzhao held firm and did not comply, saying, 'Your Majesty can pardon him yourself — how can you have me bend the brush?'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Youzhao was chief of the Court of Judicial Review. The emperor privately ordered Youzhao to reduce or pardon someone. Youzhao held firm and did not comply, saying, 'Your Majesty can pardon him yourself — how can you have me bend the brush?'

sentences.zh: 」又言：「為國當以嚴致平，非以寬致平。

translations.literal: " He also said: "To govern a state one should achieve peace through strictness, not through leniency."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "To govern a state one should achieve peace through strictness, not through leniency."

sentences.zh: 嚴者，非凝網重罰，在人不易犯而防難越也。

translations.literal: Strictness does not mean tightening the net with heavy punishments; it means that people do not easily offend and are prevented from transgressing.
translations.idiomatic: Strictness does not mean tightening the net with heavy punishments. It means that people do not easily offend and are prevented from transgressing.

sentences.zh: 故舍銜策於奔馳，則王良不能禦駻；

translations.literal: Therefore if one removes the bit and whip during a gallop, even Wang Liang cannot control a wild horse;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if one removes the bit and whip during a gallop, even Wang Liang cannot control a wild horse;

sentences.zh: 停藥石於膚腠，則俞附不能攻疾。」

translations.literal: if one stops medicine at the skin, then Yu Fu cannot cure the illness.
translations.idiomatic: if one stops medicine at the skin, then Yu Fu cannot cure the illness.

sentences.zh: 又言：「漢武帝甥昭平君殺人，以公主子，廷尉上請，帝垂涕曰：『法令者，先帝之所造也，用親故誣先帝法，吾何面目入高廟乎？』

translations.literal: He also said: "Emperor Wu of Han's nephew Zhao Pingjun killed a man; as the princess's son the chief of the Court of Judicial Review submitted the request; the Emperor wept and said, 'Laws and ordinances were made by the Former Emperor; to use kinship to deceive the Former Emperor's law — with what face can I enter the High Temple?'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Emperor Wu of Han's nephew Zhao Pingjun killed a man. As the princess's son the chief of the Court of Judicial Review submitted the request. The emperor wept and said, 'Laws and ordinances were made by the Former Emperor. To use kinship to deceive the Former Emperor's law — with what face can I enter the High Temple?'

sentences.zh: 卒可其奏。

translations.literal: He finally approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He finally approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝子秦王俊為并州總管，以奢縱免官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui's son Qin Jun was area commander of Bingzhou and was dismissed from office for extravagance and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui's son Qin Jun was area commander of Bing Prefecture and was dismissed from office for extravagance and indulgence.

sentences.zh: 楊素曰：『王，陛下愛子，請赦之。』

translations.literal: Yang Su said, 'The prince is Your Majesty's beloved son — please pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su said, 'The prince is Your Majesty's beloved son — please pardon him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：『法不可違，若如公意，我乃五兒之父，非兆人之父，何不別制天子子律乎？』

translations.literal: The Emperor said, 'The law cannot be violated. If I followed your wish I would be father to my five sons alone, not father to the myriad people — why not make a separate law for the Son of Heaven's sons?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'The law cannot be violated. If I followed your wish I would be father to my five sons alone, not father to the myriad people — why not make a separate law for the Son of Heaven's sons?

sentences.zh: 故天子操法有不變之義。」

translations.literal: Therefore in wielding the law the Son of Heaven has the meaning of unchanging principle."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in wielding the law the Son of Heaven has the meaning of unchanging principle."

sentences.zh: 凡數千言，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: In all several thousand words; the Emperor commended it.
translations.idiomatic: In all several thousand words; the emperor commended it.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，以左御史中丞遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he was transferred from left assistant censor-in-chief to vice chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingyun period he was transferred from left assistant censor-in-chief to vice chief of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時詔用漢故事，設刺史監郡，於天下劇州置都督，選素威重者授之。

translations.literal: At the time an edict followed Han precedent to establish regional inspectors to supervise commanderies and to place area commanders in the most important prefectures throughout the empire, selecting men of established authority and weight to appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict followed Han precedent to establish regional inspectors to supervise commanderies and to place area commanders in the most important prefectures throughout the empire, selecting men of established authority and weight to appoint them.

sentences.zh: 遂拜誌愔齊州都督，事中格，復授齊州刺史、河南道按察使。

translations.literal: Zhiyin was then appointed area commander of Qi; the arrangement was blocked mid-course; he was again appointed prefect of Qi and inspecting commissioner of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyin was then appointed area commander of Qi, but the arrangement was blocked mid-course. He was again appointed prefect of Qi and inspecting commissioner of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 徙汴州，封北海縣男。

translations.literal: He was moved to Bian Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Beihai county.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Bian Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Beihai County.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，兼御史中丞內供奉，實封百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji he also served as assistant censor-in-chief on inner palace duty, with a substantive fief of a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiji he also served as assistant censor-in-chief on inner palace duty, with a substantive fief of a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為魏州刺史，改揚州長史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Wei and changed to chief administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Wei and then made chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 所至破碎奸猾，令行禁信，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he shattered the cunning and corrupt; orders were carried out and prohibitions trusted; within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he shattered the cunning and corrupt. Orders were carried out and prohibitions trusted, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，帝幸東都，詔留守京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan the Emperor visited the eastern capital and ordered him to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan the emperor visited the eastern capital and ordered him to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 京兆人權梁山妄稱襄王子，與左右屯營官謀反，自稱光帝，夜犯長樂門，入宮城，將殺誌愔，誌愔逾垣走，而屯營兵悔，更斬梁山等自歸，誌愔慚悸卒。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao man Quan Liangshan falsely claimed to be a son of Prince Xiang; he plotted rebellion with officers of the Left and Right Garrison Camps; he styled himself Emperor Guang; at night he attacked Changle Gate and entered the palace city intending to kill Zhiyin; Zhiyin climbed over the wall and fled; the garrison troops repented, beheaded Liangshan and the others and surrendered themselves; Zhiyin died of shame and fright.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao man Quan Liangshan falsely claimed to be a son of Prince Xiang and plotted rebellion with officers of the Left and Right Garrison Camps. He styled himself Emperor Guang. At night he attacked Changle Gate and entered the palace city intending to kill Zhiyin. Zhiyin climbed over the wall and fled. The garrison troops repented, beheaded Liangshan and the others, and surrendered themselves. Zhiyin died of shame and fright.

sentences.zh: =許景先=許景先，常州義興人。

translations.literal: Xu Jingxian. Xu Jingxian was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingxian. Xu Jingxian came from Yixing in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖緒，武德時以佐命功，歷左散騎常侍，封真定公，遂家洛陽。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xu was, in the Wude era for merit in assisting the founding mandate, left regular attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhending; the family then settled in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xu, for merit in assisting the founding mandate during the Wude period, served as left regular attendant and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhending. The family then settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 景先由進士第釋褐夏陽尉。

translations.literal: Jingxian through placing in the jinshi examination left the commoner's garb as aide at Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian passed the jinshi examination and entered service as aide at Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，東都造服慈閣，景先獻賦，李迥秀見其文，畏嘆曰：「是宜付太史！」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the eastern capital built the Fuci Pavilion; Jingxian submitted a fu-rhapsody; Li Jiongxiu saw his writing and in awe exclaimed, "This should be handed to the grand astrologer!"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong period the eastern capital built the Fuci Pavilion. Jingxian submitted a fu-rhapsody. Li Jiongxiu saw his writing and in awe exclaimed, "This should be handed to the grand astrologer!"

sentences.zh: 擢左拾遺，以論事切直，外補滑州司士參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left remonstrator; because his policy discussions were sharp and direct he was sent out to supplement as military adjutant in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left remonstrator. Because his policy discussions were sharp and direct he was sent out as military adjutant in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉手筆俊拔、茂才異等連中，進揚州兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: He passed in succession the examinations for outstanding brushwork and for extraordinary talent and was advanced to military adjutant in Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed in succession the examinations for outstanding brushwork and for extraordinary talent and was advanced to military adjutant in Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還為左補闕。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as left rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as left rectifier.

sentences.zh: 宋璟、蘇颋擇殿中侍御史，久不補，以授景先，時議僉愜。

translations.literal: Song Jing and Su Ting chose an attending censor within the palace; the post had long gone unfilled; they gave it to Jingxian, and public opinion was entirely satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Su Ting chose an attending censor within the palace. The post had long gone unfilled, and they gave it to Jingxian. Public opinion was entirely satisfied.

sentences.zh: 抨按不避近強。

translations.literal: In impeachment and investigation he did not avoid the powerful nearby.
translations.idiomatic: In impeachment and investigation he did not avoid the powerful nearby.

sentences.zh: 與齊浣、王丘、韓休、張九齡更知制誥，以雅厚稱。

translations.literal: He alternated with Qi Huan, Wang Qiu, Han Xiu, and Zhang Jiuling in drafting edicts and was known for elegant depth.
translations.idiomatic: He alternated with Qi Huan, Wang Qiu, Han Xiu, and Zhang Jiuling in drafting edicts and was known for elegant depth.

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「許舍人之文，雖乏峻峰激流，然詞旨豐美，得中和之氣。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said, "Attendant Xu Jingxian's writing, though lacking sharp peaks and rushing currents, has rich and beautiful diction and attains the spirit of centrality and harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said, "Attendant Xu Jingxian's writing, though lacking sharp peaks and rushing currents, has rich and beautiful diction and attains the spirit of centrality and harmony."

sentences.zh: 開元十年，伊、汝溢，壞廬舍甚眾，景先見侍中源乾曜曰：「災眚所降，王者宜修德應之，因遣大臣存問失職，罪己引咎，以答天譴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan the Yi and Ru rivers overflowed and destroyed many dwellings; Jingxian saw Chief Minister Yuan Qianyao and said, "When calamities descend, the king should cultivate virtue to respond, send great ministers to inquire after those who have lost their livelihoods, confess faults and accept blame, to answer heaven's rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan the Yi and Ru rivers overflowed and destroyed many dwellings. Jingxian saw Chief Minister Yuan Qianyao and said, "When calamities descend, the king should cultivate virtue to respond, send great ministers to inquire after those who have lost their livelihoods, confess faults and accept blame, to answer heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 公在元弼，庸可默乎？」

translations.literal: You are among the chief ministers — can you remain silent?"
translations.idiomatic: You are among the chief ministers — can you remain silent?"

sentences.zh: 乾曜悟，遽白玄宗，遣陸象先持節賑贍。

translations.literal: Qianyao understood, immediately reported to Xuanzong, and sent Lu Xiangxian bearing credentials to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao understood, immediately reported to Emperor Xuanzong, and sent Lu Xiangxian bearing credentials to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝自擇刺史，景先由吏部侍郎為刺史治虢州，大理卿源光裕鄭州，兵部侍郎寇泚宋州，禮部侍郎鄭溫琦邠州，大理少卿袁仁敬杭州，鴻臚少卿崔誌廉襄州，衛尉少卿李升期邢州，太仆少卿鄭放定州，國子司業蔣挺湖州，左衛將軍裴觀滄州，衛率崔誠遂州，凡十一人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Emperor personally chose prefects: Jingxian from vice minister of personnel became prefect governing Guo; Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Guangyu, Zheng; Vice Minister of War Kou Ci, Song; Vice Minister of Rites Zheng Wenqi, Bin; Vice Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Renjing, Hang; Vice Minister of Ceremonial Cui Zhilian, Xiang; Vice Minister of the Guard Li Shengqi, Xing; Vice Minister of the Stud Zheng Fang, Ding; Vice Rector of the Directorate of Education Jiang Ting, Hu; General of the Left Guard Pei Guan, Cang; Guard Commander Cui Cheng, Su — eleven men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor personally chose prefects: Jingxian from vice minister of personnel became prefect of Guo; Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Guangyu, Zheng; Vice Minister of War Kou Ci, Song; Vice Minister of Rites Zheng Wenqi, Bin; Vice Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Renjing, Hang; Vice Minister of Ceremonial Cui Zhilian, Xiang; Vice Minister of the Guard Li Shengqi, Xing; Vice Minister of the Stud Zheng Fang, Ding; Vice Rector of the Directorate of Education Jiang Ting, Hu; General of the Left Guard Pei Guan, Cang; Guard Commander Cui Cheng, Su — eleven men in all.

sentences.zh: 治行，詔宰相、諸王、御史以上祖道洛濱，盛具，奏太常樂，帛舫水嬉，命高力士賜詩，帝親書，且給筆紙令自賦，賚絹三千遣之。

translations.literal: When they were about to depart, an edict ordered the chief ministers, princes, and censors and above to give them a send-off at the Luo riverbank with lavish provisions; the Music Bureau performed; silk boats sported on the water; Gao Lishi was ordered to bestow poems; the Emperor personally wrote and also provided brush and paper for them to compose themselves; three thousand bolts of silk were granted and they were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to depart, an edict ordered the chief ministers, princes, and censors and above to give them a send-off at the Luo riverbank with lavish provisions. The Music Bureau performed, silk boats sported on the water, and Gao Lishi was ordered to bestow poems. The emperor personally wrote and also provided brush and paper for them to compose themselves. Three thousand bolts of silk were granted and they were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 後徙岐州，入為吏部侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Qi Prefecture, entered office as vice minister of personnel, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was moved to Qi Prefecture, entered office as vice minister of personnel, and died.

sentences.zh: =潘好禮=潘好禮，貝州宗城人。

translations.literal: Pan Haoli. Pan Haoli was a native of Zongcheng in Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Haoli. Pan Haoli came from Zongcheng in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第明經，累遷上蔡令，治在最，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination, was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Shangcai, his governance ranked highest, and was advanced to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination, rose through repeated promotions to magistrate of Shangcai, ranked highest in governance, and was advanced to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 坐小累，下除芮城令，拜侍御史，徙岐王府司馬。

translations.literal: For a minor offense he was demoted to magistrate of Ruicheng, appointed attending censor, and transferred to military aide of the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: For a minor offense he was demoted to magistrate of Ruicheng, appointed attending censor, and transferred to military aide of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 居後母喪，詔奪服，固辭不出。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his stepmother an edict ordered him to leave mourning garb; he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his stepmother he was ordered by edict to leave mourning garb, but he firmly declined and did not take office.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為邠王府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he became chief administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan period he became chief administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.

sentences.zh: 王為滑州刺史，好禮兼府司馬、知州事。

translations.literal: When the prince became prefect of Hua, Haoli also served as military aide of the princely household and managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became prefect of Hua, Haoli also served as military aide of the princely household and managed prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 王禦下不能肅，有詔好禮檢督王家，至過失皆上聞。

translations.literal: The prince could not keep his subordinates in order; an edict ordered Haoli to inspect and supervise the princely household, and all faults were reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prince could not keep his subordinates in order. An edict ordered Haoli to inspect and supervise the princely household, and all faults were reported upward.

sentences.zh: 王每遊觀，好禮必諫諭禁切。

translations.literal: Whenever the prince went sightseeing Haoli always remonstrated and admonished with strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince went sightseeing Haoli always remonstrated and admonished with strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 農月，王出獵，家奴羅迾，好禮遮道諫，王初不許，乃臥馬下呼曰：「今農在田，王何得非時暴禾稼，以損下人？

translations.literal: In the farming month the prince went hunting; household slaves cordoned the way; Haoli blocked the road and remonstrated; the prince at first would not agree; Haoli then lay beneath the horse and cried, "Now the farmers are in the fields — how can Your Highness at the wrong season trample the grain and harm the common people?
translations.idiomatic: During the farming month the prince went hunting. Household slaves cordoned the way. Haoli blocked the road and remonstrated, but the prince at first would not agree. Haoli then lay beneath the horse and cried, "The farmers are in the fields now — how can Your Highness at the wrong season trample the grain and harm the common people?

sentences.zh: 要先踐殺司馬，然後聽所為！」

translations.literal: You must first trample me, the military aide, to death — then do as you please!"
translations.idiomatic: You must first trample me, the military aide, to death — then do as you please!"

sentences.zh: 王慚，為還。

translations.literal: The prince was ashamed and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was ashamed and turned back.

sentences.zh: 遷豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 勤力於治，清廉無所私，然喜察細事，下厭其苛。

translations.literal: He worked hard at governance and was incorruptible without private interest, yet he liked to investigate petty matters, and subordinates resented his severity.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard at governance and was incorruptible without private interest, yet he liked to investigate petty matters, and subordinates resented his severity.

sentences.zh: 子請舉明經，好禮曰：「經不明，不可妄進。」

translations.literal: His son asked to take the Mingjing examination; Haoli said, "If the classics are not understood, one must not rashly advance."
translations.idiomatic: His son asked to take the Mingjing examination. Haoli said, "If the classics are not understood, one must not rashly advance."

sentences.zh: 乃自試之，不能通，怒笞之，械而徇於門。

translations.literal: He then tested him himself; the son could not pass; enraged, he flogged him, put him in cangue, and displayed him at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then tested him himself. The son could not pass, so enraged he flogged him, put him in cangue, and displayed him at the gate.

sentences.zh: 復以公累，徙溫州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: Again for a public offense he was moved to assistant administrator of Wen Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Again for a public offense he was moved to assistant administrator of Wen Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 好禮博學，能論議，節行修整，一意無所傾附。

translations.literal: Haoli was broadly learned and able in debate; his conduct was disciplined and correct; he held to one purpose and leaned toward no faction.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli was broadly learned and able in debate. His conduct was disciplined and correct, and he held to one purpose without leaning toward any faction.

sentences.zh: 未嘗自列階勛，居室服用粗茍至終身，世謂近名。

translations.literal: He never listed his own rank and merit; his dwelling and dress were coarse and plain to the end of his life; the age said he courted reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He never listed his own rank and merit. His dwelling and dress were coarse and plain to the end of his life, and contemporaries said he courted reputation.

sentences.zh: =倪若水=倪若水，字子泉，恒州槁城人。

translations.literal: Ni Ruoshui. Ni Ruoshui, courtesy name Ziquan, was a native of Gaocheng in Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Ruoshui. Ni Ruoshui, courtesy name Ziquan, came from Gaocheng in Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，累遷右臺監察御史。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and after repeated promotions became investigating censor of the right censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and after repeated promotions became investigating censor of the right censorate.

sentences.zh: 黜陟劍南道，繩舉嚴允，課第一。

translations.literal: As promotion-and-demotion commissioner on the Jiannan circuit he investigated and reported with strict fairness; his assessment ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: As promotion-and-demotion commissioner on the Jiannan circuit he investigated and reported with strict fairness, and his assessment ranked first.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為中書舍人、尚書右丞，出為汴州刺史，政清凈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was drafting secretary of the Secretariat and right vice minister of the ministries; he was sent out as prefect of Bian; his governance was pure and clean.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan period he was drafting secretary of the Secretariat and right vice minister of the ministries. He was sent out as prefect of Bian, where his governance was pure and clean.

sentences.zh: 增修孔子廟，興州縣學廬，勸生徒，身為教誨，風化興行。

translations.literal: He expanded and repaired the Confucius temple, established district and county schools, encouraged students, personally taught and instructed, and civilizing transformation flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded and repaired the Confucius temple, established district and county schools, encouraged students, and personally taught and instructed until civilizing transformation flourished.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣中人捕鵁鶄、鸂鶒南方，若水上言：「農方田，婦方蠶，以此時捕奇禽怪羽為園禦之玩，自江、嶺而南，達京師，水舟陸賫，所飼魚蟲、稻粱，道路之言，不以賤人貴鳥望陛下邪？」

translations.literal: Xuanzong sent palace agents to capture jacanas and grebes in the south; Ruoshui memorialized: "Farmers are in the fields and women are raising silkworms — to capture strange birds at this season for garden and imperial amusement, from the Yangzi and Ling ranges southward to the capital, by water and land transport, feeding fish, insects, rice, and grain — do the people on the roads not look to Your Majesty to value men over birds?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent palace agents to capture jacanas and grebes in the south. Ruoshui memorialized: "Farmers are in the fields and women are raising silkworms. To capture strange birds at this season for garden and imperial amusement, from the Yangzi and Ling ranges southward to the capital by water and land transport, feeding fish, insects, rice, and grain — do the people on the roads not look to Your Majesty to value men over birds?"

sentences.zh: 帝手詔褒答，悉放所玩，謫使人過取罪，而賜若水帛四十段。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally wrote an edict in praise and reply, released all the captured birds, punished the agents for overreaching, and bestowed forty bolts of silk on Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote an edict in praise and reply, released all the captured birds, punished the agents for overreaching, and bestowed forty bolts of silk on Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 時天下久平，朝廷尊榮，人皆重內任，雖自冗官擢方面，皆自謂下遷。

translations.literal: At the time the empire had long been at peace and the court was honored and glorious; all valued inner appointments; even when promoted from redundant posts to regional command, all considered it a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had long been at peace and the court was honored and glorious. All valued inner appointments, and even when promoted from redundant posts to regional command, all considered it a demotion.

sentences.zh: 班景倩自揚州采訪使入為大理少卿，過州，若水餞於郊，顧左右曰：「班公是行若登仙，吾恨不得為騶仆。」

translations.literal: Ban Jingqian entered office from Yangzhou investigating commissioner as vice chief of the Court of Judicial Review; passing through the prefecture Ruoshui saw him off in the suburbs and said to those beside him, "Master Ban's journey this time is like ascending to immortality — I regret I cannot be his outrider and groom."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Jingqian entered office from Yangzhou investigating commissioner as vice chief of the Court of Judicial Review. Passing through the prefecture, Ruoshui saw him off in the suburbs and said to those beside him, "Master Ban's journey this time is like ascending to immortality — I regret I cannot be his outrider and groom."

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為戶部侍郎，復拜右丞，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he entered office as vice minister of revenue, was again appointed right vice minister, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered office as vice minister of revenue, was again appointed right vice minister, and died.

sentences.zh: =席豫=席豫，字建侯，襄州襄陽人。

translations.literal: Xi Yu. Xi Yu, courtesy name Jianhou, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yu. Xi Yu, courtesy name Jianhou, came from Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
